section_1.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
section_1.content: Briefly review Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) as a 'single-path' relationship. Introduce PDEs as systems with multiple independent variables (space and time). Use an animation showing a line evolving vs. a 2D surface morphing.
section_1.example: Comparing a swinging pendulum (ODE - time only) to the vibration of a drum skin (PDE - time and 2D surface coordinates).

section_2.title: The Heat Equation: Diffusion in Motion
section_2.content: Introduce the Heat Equation as the fundamental PDE for spatial change. Explain the 'concavity' concept—heat flows from hot spots to cold spots. Use a thermal gradient color map animation.
section_2.example: A cat sleeping on a cold floor; the heat transfer from the cat's body to the floor tiles over time.

section_3.title: The Wave Equation: Ripples and Rhythm
section_3.content: Focus on the second-order partial derivative with respect to time. Visualize how a local disturbance (a poke) triggers a wave propagation. Emphasize that speed depends on the medium.
section_3.example: A robotic arm striking a guitar string; the animation shows the wave packet traveling back and forth along the string.

section_4.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions: Defining the System
section_4.content: Explain that PDEs describe 'infinite' possibilities. We need Initial Conditions (snapshot at t=0) and Boundary Conditions (what happens at the edges) to pin down a specific solution.
section_4.example: Simulating the water level in an aquarium (PDE) based on the shape of the tank (Boundary) and the initial splash (Initial).

section_5.title: Summary and Real-world Impact
section_5.content: Synthesize the logic: Variables -> Operators -> Constraints -> Solution. Conclude with how PDEs power weather forecasting and movie special effects.
section_5.example: Visualizing a 'fire simulation' in a video game, where PDEs calculate the spread of flames across a 3D environment.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.2
                y = 2.0 - i * 1.0
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject
